[MUJAHID:v2p429/r1] MUJAHID, d. 104 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid reports that God planted the Gardens of Eden by His hand, closed them when complete, and looks at them each dawn; they say, 'The believers have succeeded.'
[MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said Firdaws was created and planted by God's hand, incomparable to anything seen or imagined, then commanded to adorn itself twice and speak; it declared that the believers prospered. | mentions 23:1
[MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · ابن عباس | reports | The Prophet's report says Firdaws named the successful as the monotheists of Muhammad's community, who inherit Firdaws eternally. | mentions 23:10, 23:11
[MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r7] MUQATIL, d. 150 · ابن عباس | reports | The report says Firdaws's gate stays closed until Resurrection, its fragrance and houris are at its entrance, and the Prophet waits at the Pool to turn away unbelievers and recognize his community by ablution's light.
[MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r8] MUQATIL, d. 150 · ابن عباس | reports | The Prophet said whoever drinks from his Pool will never thirst again; Muadh called such drinkers fortunate, and the Prophet said a monotheist who believes in the messenger drinks and enters Firdaws.
[MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r9] MUQATIL, d. 150 · ابن عباس | reports | The Prophet told Muadh that those who die Muslim were created Muslim in Adam, passed through unbelieving ancestors until they believed in him, and are his brothers, while his contemporaries are his companions.
[MUQATIL:23:1-6/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The believers have prospered, meaning they have become happy; believers here are those who affirm God's oneness.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The believers have prospered by becoming happy; the happy ones are the people of Paradise.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r2] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · كعب | reports | Ka'b says God made only Adam, the Torah, and Paradise with His hand; He told Paradise to speak, and it spoke this verse.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · المعلى بن هلال | reports | Al-Mu'alla reports that God built Paradise with gold and silver bricks and musk mortar, filled it, spoke this verse, then closed it so no angel or prophet knows what is inside; the dawn's coolness and scent escape through its door.
[ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43/r1] ABDURRAZZAQ, d. 211 · كعب | reports | Kaʿb says God created three things with His hand: Adam, the Torah, and the Garden of Eden; when the Garden was told to speak, it said believers have prospered, knowing their honor with God.
[TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The believers succeed by believing God and His Messenger, accepting the revelation, and doing the acts named in these verses; their reward is lasting Gardens and fulfillment of their hopes with God.
[TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · كعب | reports | Kaʿb says God made Adam, wrote the Torah, and planted Eden by His hand; when told to speak, the Garden said the verse, knowing the honor within it.
[TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says God planted the Garden, looked at it, and said the verse.
[TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أبو العالية | reports | Abu al-ʿAliya says that when God created the Garden He said the verse, which He then revealed in the Qurʾan.
[TAB-FULL:v17p5#2/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ميسرة | reports | Maysara says God created four things by His hand—Adam, the Tablets, the Torah, and Eden—and then said the verse.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The sura is Meccan.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The believers have attained lasting continuance in goodness; an alternate reading means they were brought to success.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r3] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · كعب الحبر | reports | Kaʿb al-Aḥbār reports that God created Adam, the Garden of Eden, and the Torah with His hand; when told to speak, Eden said قد أفلح المؤمنون on seeing its inhabitants' honors.
[ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r4] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Believers affirm what came from God, His oneness without partner, and that Muhammad is His prophet.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p147/r12] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · ورش عن نافع | holds | Warsh transfers the hamza’s vowel to the preceding consonant and drops it, both within words and across word boundaries. | mentions 23:1, 28:71
[NAHHAS:v3p109/r1] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | In the softened reading of قد أفلح, the hamza’s vowel moves to the preceding sukūn-bearing dāl, then the hamza drops to avoid adjacent sukūns.
[SULAMI:v2p30#2/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · أحمد بن عاصم الأنطاكي | reports | The believer’s treasure is his Lord, his aversion is this world, his beloved is the hereafter, his provision is piety, and his gathering is remembrance.
[SULAMI:v2p30#2/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | Success is reaching the highest station of nearness and happiness through affirming God’s promise.
[SULAMI:v2p30#2/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | A believer is trustworthy with heart, spirit, secret, and limbs; faith entails integrity outwardly and inwardly.
[SULAMI:v2p30#2/r4] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو بكر بن طاهر | reports | A believer is safe for himself and others, welcomes and comforts people, and his company is solace for believers, mercy for seekers, and counsel for the pious.
[THALABI:v7p37#3/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Qad emphasizes the statement and brings a past event close to the present: believers’ success has happened and continues, a stronger description than simply mentioning success.
[THALABI:v7p37#3/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Falāḥ means success and lasting continuance.
[THALABI:v7p37#3/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas reports that the Garden of Eden spoke when God commanded it, saying ‘the believers have succeeded’ three times and barring misers and show-offs.
[THALABI:v7p37#3/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · طلحة بن مصرف | reports | Talha ibn Musarrif reads the verb passively: believers were made successful in their reward.
[THALABI:v7p41/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | Umar reports that revelation sounded like bees; after praying for increase, honor, and favor, the Prophet said whoever establishes the ten revealed verses enters Paradise and recited the opening ten verses of this sura.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | One lexical explanation is that aflaha means to be happy or succeed; Labid's verse is cited as evidence.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | A second explanation is lasting: the believers' deeds endure or they abide in Paradise; the call to prayer and poetry support this sense of lasting good.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p44#2/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | A third explanation is attaining one's aims, illustrated by a poet's line about Mulaʿib al-Rimah attaining falah.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas defines the successful as those who attain what they seek and escape the evil from which they flee.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | ʿUmar reports that revelation sounded like a bee's drone near the Prophet; the Prophet then prayed for increase, honor, giving, preference, and God's approval, and said whoever upholds these ten verses enters Paradise.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · أبو عمران الجوني | reports | Abu ʿImran al-Jawni reports that Aisha had al-Muʾminun recited through “they guard their prayers,” then said that this was the Prophet's character.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r1] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The name derives from elevation; the named one deserves loftiness, and the Real is true through primordial loftiness.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Knowing Bismillah raises a person’s aspiration and brings the heart knowledge whose cause is unknown to it.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Falāḥ means reaching what one seeks and attaining one’s intended goal.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r4] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Faith is truth taking root in the inner self, affirmation permeating the heart’s core, and realization settling in the heart.
[WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1] WAHIDI-ASBAB, d. 468 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | Umar describes revelation’s bee-like sound and the Prophet’s supplication, then reports that whoever upholds the first ten verses of al-Muʾminun enters Paradise.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الليث | reports | Al-Layth says قد is a particle that affirms an occurrence, adding emphasis to the truth of the statement.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · النحويون | reports | Grammarians say قد can bring a past verb close to the present, as in قد قامت الصلاة.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الشاعر | reports | The cited poem, أم صبي قد حبا أو دارج, likewise uses قد with a past form as a current state: crawling or toddling.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra says a past verb used as a circumstantial clause requires قد, stated or understood, as in 4:90. | mentions 4:90
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Here قد may emphasize the believers’ success or bring the past close to the present: their success has been attained and remains theirs now.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the believers have attained felicity and remain in Paradise.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abu Ishaq explains their success as attaining everlasting life.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p517/r8] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · رسول الله | reports | Humayd reports from Anas that the Prophet said God created and planted the Garden of Eden, told it to speak, and it said the believers had succeeded; the source gives no grading.

[JISHUMI:v7p5017/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبي بن كعب | reports | Ubayy ibn Kaʿb transmits from the Prophet that reciting the sūra brings angels’ glad tidings of comfort and delight at the time of death.
[JISHUMI:v7p5017/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · عمر | reports | In a long report from the Prophet, ʿUmar says that whoever upholds ten verses enters Paradise, then the Prophet recited this sūra’s opening.

[JISHUMI:v7p5018/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | فلاح means success or lasting life; Arabs call anyone who attains good a successful person.

[JISHUMI:v7p5018/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قراءة العامة | reports | The common reading has a fatḥa on the initial alif; Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif has a passive form meaning they were cast into the earth.
[JISHUMI:v7p5018/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | قد emphasizes a statement; ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says it brings a past event close to the present, making success already attained and continuing.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The verses reserve Paradise and its reward for believers, refuting Murjiʾites who say a grave sinner attains it.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | A believer attains the object of his or her desire.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The term believer is a commendatory name and should not be applied to a sinner deserving punishment.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | Another view is that believer is a technical name established by religious law.
[JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The listed traits remove ambiguity: whoever has them is a believer, supporting the author’s position.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | ʿUmar reports that revelation sounded like a buzzing bee near the Prophet’s face; after a pause the Prophet faced the qibla, raised his hands, prayed for generous divine favor, and said that whoever establishes ten verses beginning with this opening will enter the Garden.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · أحمد بن حنبل وعلي بن المديني وجماعة | reports | Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, and others transmit a variant prayer wording that adds a request to be made content, alongside the request for God’s pleasure.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The particle qad is an emphatic particle.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · المحققون | reports | Qad brings the past close to the present, indicating that believers have attained success and remain in it; this is more emphatic than stating the verb alone.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Al-falah means salvation and enduring life; Ibn Abbas explains that those affirming divine oneness are blessed and remain in Paradise.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the believers who affirm God's oneness attain felicity and remain in Paradise.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Qad affirms an expected outcome while lammā denies it; it establishes the success believers awaited.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | Falāḥ means attaining one’s aim or remaining in goodness; aflaḥa means entering success, and aflaḥahu making someone succeed.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · طلحة بن مصرف | reports | Ṭalḥa reads aflaḥa passive, aflaḥū by the ‘akalūnī al-barāghīth’ construction or ellipsis, and aflaḥ with ḍamma instead of wāw, supported by poetry.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | In language, a believer is one who confirms.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r5] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | One legal view counts anyone professing the testimonies with heart and tongue aligned as a believer; another reserves the praise for the righteous and pious, excluding sinners.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The believers succeeded by attaining their goal and securing lasting continuance.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · كعب الأحبار | reports | Kaʿb al-Aḥbār reports that when God created the Garden of Eden and asked it to speak, it said that the believers had succeeded.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid reports that after creating and perfecting the Garden, God declared that the believers had succeeded.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · طلحة بن مصرف | rejects | Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif's reading with ḍamma on ḥāʾ intends afl aḥū, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects it.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · طلحة بن مصرف | reports | Another reading reported from Ṭalḥa has ḍamma on hamza and kasra on lām.
[TABRISI:23:1-3/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Those who believe in God’s oneness and His messengers have won God’s reward.
[TABRISI:23:1-3/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | One explanation gives aflaḥ the sense of remaining: the believers’ good deeds have endured.
[TABRISI:23:1-3/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Another explanation gives aflaḥ the sense of becoming happy or prosperous; Labid’s line is cited as evidence.
[TABRISI:23:1-3/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farraʾ says qad confirms success or brings a past event near the present, as when the prayer call precedes prayer.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · عمر بن الخطاب عن رسول الله | reports | Umar reports the Prophet saying ten verses were revealed: whoever upholds them enters Paradise; he recited from this verse through ten verses. Al-Hakim included it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله | reports | Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet describing Paradise's gold and silver wall and its planted tree, which proclaimed that the believers prosper; he said, Blessed is your home, abode of kings.

[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الفراء | reports | Alternatively, qad brings the past close to the present, as in announcing that the prayer has begun before it actually begins.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The verse presents success as already attained and still true of the believers now.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبي بن كعب وعكرمة وعاصم الجحدري وطلحة بن مصرف | reports | These readers pronounce the verb in the passive: the believers have been brought to success.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj explains success as attaining lasting permanence in goodness.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p458/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | With the passive reading, the meaning is that the believers were made to attain success.
[RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | God promises success to those who combine seven qualities; the segment begins explaining those qualities with “the believers.”
[RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | “Qad” contrasts with “lammā”: it affirms an expected event, here the believers’ anticipated glad tidings that success is firmly theirs.
[RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Falāḥ means attaining one’s desired end, or remaining in good; aflaha can mean entering success, as abshara means entering glad tidings, or it can be causative, “he made him succeed.”
[RAZI-FULL:v23p67/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · طلحة بن مصرف | reports | Talha ibn Musarrif read aflaha in the passive; a further form aflaha is attributed to him either by the “akalūnī al-barāghīth” dialect or by an indefinite verb followed by an explanatory subject.

[RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r10] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | God's creating the Garden with His hand means He personally undertook its creation rather than delegating it.
[RAZI-FULL:v23p72#2/r11] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Prayer's praise is figurative: prayer consists of movements and stillnesses that cannot literally take form and speak, like saying a benefactor's kindness speaks gratitude.

[TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The traits in the opening passage show faith as living and active, producing its effects so that the believer reaches the intended end, success.
[TABATABAI:23:1-11/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Religion is a social way of life based on beliefs about the universe and humanity; social customs and laws therefore vary with those beliefs.
[TABATABAI:23:1-11/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Those who believe in a Lord as the universe's source and return, and in enduring human life, shape conduct toward lasting happiness in the afterlife.
[TABATABAI:23:1-11/r6] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Those who affirm deities governing through favor and displeasure but no return to God organize life to please them and gain worldly goods and desires.
[TABATABAI:23:1-11/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Materialists, who disregard lordship and deny lasting human life, base social laws on enjoyment of the finite life ending at death.
[TABATABAI:23:1-11/r8] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Theoretical knowledge about God and humanity does not itself direct action; faith is practical knowledge or judgment that one must follow what that knowledge entails.
[TABATABAI:23:1-11/r9] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Religious preaching addresses practical commitment to true belief in God, messengers, the Last Day, and revelation, including worship and conduct for happiness in both lives.
[TABATABAI:23:1/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The Meccan sura calls people to believe in God and the Last Day, contrasts believers’ fine servitude with disbelievers’ vices, then gives glad tidings and warnings including the annihilation of denying peoples from Noah through Jesus.

[TABATABAI:23:1/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Success has worldly and afterlife forms: worldly happiness includes long life, wealth, and honor; the afterlife brings permanence, freedom from poverty, freedom from disgrace, and knowledge without ignorance.
[TABATABAI:23:1/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Calling attainment falah evokes splitting through the obstacle and uncovering the face of one’s desired goal.

[TABATABAI:23:1/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Belief is not mere mental assent without commitment: faith includes settled assurance and adherence to implications, whereas knowledge can coexist with failure to abandon harmful or shameful habits.
